title: Quick Tip: CalcFields vs SetAutoCalcFields in AL
summary: FlowFields in Business Central are not stored in the database and must be calculated explicitly. The post explains two methods for calculating them: CalcFields for one-time calculations on single records, and SetAutoCalcFields for automatic calculation during record retrieval, with guidance on which to use to avoid performance issues.
key_points: CalcFields explicitly calculates FlowFields on the current record when called and is suitable for single-record calculations outside loops
SetAutoCalcFields automatically calculates specified FlowFields for every record retrieved during FindSet or loop iterations, improving performance over repeated CalcFields calls
Calling SetAutoCalcFields without parameters clears the auto-calculation list for the record variable
SetAutoCalcFields is scoped to the record variable, not the table, so different variables do not inherit the setting
As of BC26 (AL runtime 15.0), SetAutoCalcFields is available on RecordRef, enabling generic code to use the same pattern

quotes.text: Inside a loop, calling CalcFields on every iteration means a separate database call per record.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the key performance problem that SetAutoCalcFields solves

quotes.text: Use SetAutoCalcFields before any loop where you need a FlowField on every record.
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides the main guideline for correct usage to achieve optimal performance
